scenario:
Ravi Traders, a GST-registered business in Maharashtra, made the following supplies during October 2024:
• Intra-state sales of taxable goods: Rs. 8,00,000 (GST rate 18%)
• Inter-state sales of taxable goods: Rs. 3,00,000 (GST rate 12%)
• Export of goods (zero-rated): Rs. 1,50,000
• Sale of exempt goods: Rs. 50,000
question: Calculate the total GST output tax liability (CGST, SGST, IGST separately) for Ravi Traders for October 2024. Show your working.

scenario:

• June: Rs. 22,000

question: Determine: (a) In which month TDS first becomes applicable under Section 194C, and (b) the total TDS to be deducted by end of June. Show your working.

topic: Income Tax — LTCG on Listed Equity Shares
scenario: Arjun purchased 500 shares of XYZ Ltd. on 1 August 2022 at Rs. 240 per share. He sold all 500 shares on 15 October 2024 at Rs. 410 per share. STT was paid on both purchase and sale. Arjun has no other capital gains in FY 2024-25.
question: Calculate: (a) whether the gain is STCG or LTCG, (b) the capital gain amount, and (c) the tax payable on it.

topic: Income Tax — Deductions Under Chapter VI-A
scenario:

• ELSS mutual fund: Rs. 60,000
• Life insurance premium: Rs. 30,000
• Health insurance for self & family: Rs. 28,000

scenario:
During the GST audit of Mehta & Co. for FY 2023-24, the following mismatch is found:

As per GSTR-1: Taxable value Rs. 45,00,000 | Tax Rs. 8,10,000 (18%)
As per GSTR-3B: Taxable value Rs. 42,00,000 | Tax Rs. 7,56,000 (18%)

On investigation:
(i) Two invoices of Rs. 2,00,000 each were raised in March 2024 but not reported in GSTR-3B.
(ii) One credit note of Rs. 1,00,000 was correctly in GSTR-1 but tax reduction was double-counted in GSTR-3B.
question: Identify the nature of each discrepancy, compute the tax shortfall/excess, and state the corrective action required under GST law.
